name: Manage leverage and the funding plan
function: total fund management (treasury: balancing, liquidity and collateral)
summary: Each month the liquidity and collateral team in Total Fund Management checks how much the fund has borrowed with recourse to the parent, about C$122 billion or roughly a fifth of net assets in fiscal 2022, against the Board limit, and decides the mix of term debt, commercial paper, repo and synthetic financing the funding team should run. An associate compiles and reconciles the leverage figure after month end, the funding team reports market conditions and headroom under the authorised debt limits, and a principal projects leverage, builds funding mix options and stress-tests them against events like the March 2020 commercial paper closure. Risk reviews the recommendation, a monthly meeting chaired by a TFM managing director agrees it and the CIO approves it before the funding team turns it into an issuance calendar. Most elapsed time is waiting for month-end data and the meeting slot, and errors come from classifying derivatives and repo in the leverage figure.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian national pension fund investment manager that issues term debt and commercial paper through a guaranteed subsidiary and uses repo and derivatives to finance a diversified portfolio.
baseline.notes: Treasury duties are split: leverage and liquidity in TFM, funding execution in CMF Financing, Collateral and Trading, margin processing in Investment Operations.

unit_of_work: one monthly leverage and funding review
trigger: Month-end positions are final and the latest liquidity forecast and Risk report are available.
end_state: The CIO-approved funding plan has been sent to the funding team, turned into an execution calendar, loaded into the daily tools, reported to the Investment Risk Committee and filed.

volume.seasonality: One review a month; an extra review in stressed markets or before large term debt issues.

evidence.note: Monthly cadence from the process map; leverage is monitored daily and the Board limit reviewed yearly (F2022).

roles.title: Senior Managing Director and Chief Investment Officer

evidence.note: The CIO recommends leverage targets and approves the plan (process map). FTE from about 1 hour a month.

systems.name: SimCorp Dimension investment book of record (portfolio accounting, treasury, performance)
Risk analytics platform (potential loss, limits, stress tests)
Bloomberg terminals, market data and trade messaging
Document management and investment committee memo repository

steps.name: Month-end positions and net assets are published
steps.description: The month-end valuation run in the investment book of record publishes net assets, financing liabilities, repo balances and derivative notionals, which is what the leverage review waits for.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of the lag from month end to final positions for a fund with derivatives and repo books.

steps.name: Compile the recourse leverage position
steps.description: An associate pulls term debt by currency and maturity, commercial paper outstanding, repo and secured borrowing, and the notional of derivatives used to add exposure, nets cash and reverse repo, and computes recourse leverage as a share of net assets for each plan account.

error.defect_description: A derivative is classified as leverage-generating when it hedges, or a repo is double counted.

evidence.note: Recourse leverage is debt financing, repurchase liabilities and the notional of derivatives used to generate leverage, partly offset by cash and reverse repo. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Reconcile leverage with Risk and Finance figures
steps.description: The associate compares the workbook with the leverage figure in Risk's monthly report and the financing liabilities in the accounts, investigates any difference in classification or timing, and corrects the workbook or agrees the break with Risk.

error.defect_description: A small classification difference is left unexplained.

control.basis: Risk Policy: leverage measured consistently with the Board-approved recourse leverage definition

evidence.note: Leverage is monitored against Board limits relative to net assets. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Collect the deployment and maturity outlook
steps.description: The associate takes the latest liquidity forecast, expected private deployments and dispositions from the capital allocation guidance, plan transfer expectations and the maturity ladder of debt and repo, and lines them up by month for the next year.

error.defect_description: A large expected closing is missing from the deployment outlook.

evidence.note: Liquidity must cover debt service, collateral and margin, investment funding and rebalancing. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Report funding market conditions and capacity
steps.description: A funding principal in Financing, Collateral and Trading summarises commercial paper rates and investor demand by currency, term debt windows and new issue costs, repo capacity and haircuts by dealer, and synthetic financing costs, with remaining headroom under the authorised debt limits.

error.defect_description: Programme headroom is overstated because a pending issue is left out.

evidence.note: FCT runs the term debt programme and secured financing; authorised unsecured debt limits of C$40 billion with C$15 billion under one year. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Check collateral available for secured funding
steps.description: The liquidity principal checks in the collateral system how many unencumbered government bonds and equities are free to pledge for repo and to meet margin after current postings, since secured funding and the liquidity buffer draw on the same pool.

error.defect_description: Collateral already earmarked for margin is counted as free for repo.

evidence.note: The Balancing and Collateral group optimises collateral and delivers leverage; government bonds collateralised the term repos added in March 2020. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Project leverage against the Board limit
steps.description: The liquidity principal projects recourse leverage month by month for the next year from the funding needs, maturities and expected net asset growth, and compares the path with the Board limit and the management thresholds below it.

error.defect_description: Net asset growth assumption is optimistic, understating projected leverage.

control.basis: Board-approved leverage limit: recourse leverage at most 45% of net assets from April 2022, reviewed yearly

evidence.note: Board-level recourse leverage limit of 45% of net assets from April 1, 2022; leverage limits approved annually. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Build funding mix options
steps.description: The liquidity principal sets out two or three funding mixes for the coming months, varying term debt issuance by currency and tenor, commercial paper outstanding, repo and secured borrowing and synthetic financing, and compares all-in cost, average tenor and how much must roll over in any one month.

error.defect_description: Cost comparison ignores the repo haircut or currency swap cost.

evidence.note: Borrowed funds are term debt, commercial paper and secured borrowing, plus synthetic financing; recourse debt mix tracked by rating agencies. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Stress-test the options
steps.description: The principal runs each option through stress cases such as a closed commercial paper market, a spike in margin calls and higher repo haircuts, and checks the 10-day liquidity coverage ratio and leverage stay within limits.

error.defect_description: A stress case assumes repo can be rolled when it could not in March 2020.

evidence.note: In March 2020 large Canadian funds lost US commercial paper access and faced margin calls near C$30 billion in a week; LCR minimum 1.0x. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Risk reviews the recommendation
steps.description: A Risk director reviews the leverage projection, stress assumptions and recommended mix against the Board and management limits and sends comments or a request for changes before the meeting.

control.basis: Risk Policy: independent Risk input on leverage; IRC oversight of leverage risk limits

evidence.note: The IRC, chaired by the CFRO, guides leverage limit design and monitors exposures; Risk independently challenges the first line. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Draft the funding plan paper
steps.description: The associate turns the analysis into the monthly paper: leverage now and projected, recommended issuance and outstanding targets by instrument, stress results, Risk's comments and decisions needed.

error.defect_description: A table in the paper uses the previous run's numbers.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Hold the monthly leverage and funding review
steps.description: The TFM managing director chairs the review with the liquidity principal, the funding principal and Risk, discusses the trade-off between cost, tenor and liquidity under stress, and agrees the recommendation or asks for another option.

evidence.note: FCT works with TFM to optimise trade-offs between liquidity, financing and execution costs (F2021). Meeting cadence and times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: CIO approves the funding plan
steps.description: The Chief Investment Officer reads the agreed recommendation, asks questions on cost and stress cases and approves the funding plan, with Risk's comments attached.

control.basis: CIO accountability for recommending leverage targets and managing leverage within Board limits

evidence.note: The CIO recommends market risk and leverage targets for Board approval; TFM manages leverage. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Send the funding plan to the funding team
steps.description: The liquidity principal sends the approved plan to Financing, Collateral and Trading with the target volumes and tenors for term debt, commercial paper and secured funding and the dates by which funds are needed.

evidence.note: FCT executes the Fund's financing activities and term debt programme. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Confirm the execution calendar
steps.description: The funding principal turns the plan into an issuance calendar for term debt windows, daily commercial paper targets by currency and tenor, and repo limits by dealer, and checks each stays within the authorised debt limits.

error.defect_description: A commercial paper target would push short-term debt above the authorised limit.

control.basis: Authorised borrowing limits: unsecured debt and debt maturing within one year capped

evidence.note: Authorised unsecured debt limit C$35 billion then C$40 billion, with C$15 billion for debt maturing within a year. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Escalate projected limit pressure
steps.description: When the projection approaches the Board limit, the TFM managing director alerts the CIO and the CFRO, agrees actions such as slowing deployments, reducing synthetic exposure through balancing or terming out funding, and asks for the options to be rebuilt around them.

control.basis: Risk Policy escalation procedures for limits and thresholds

evidence.note: Breach treatment and escalation are in the Risk Policy; the IRC monitors exposures. Share and times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Update leverage targets and thresholds in tools
steps.description: The associate updates the leverage targets and instrument limits in the treasury workbook and the dashboards used daily by the liquidity and funding teams, and a colleague checks them.

error.defect_description: An outdated threshold remains in a dashboard.

control.basis: Four-eyes check of limit and threshold changes

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Prepare the leverage section for the Investment Risk Committee
steps.description: The associate writes the leverage and funding page for the Investment Risk Committee pack, showing recourse leverage against the limit, the funding mix and maturity profile and any escalation.

error.defect_description: The page shows a different leverage figure from Risk's report.

control.basis: Investment Statement s. 9.10: leverage and other key risks reported to the Board at least quarterly

evidence.note: Management reports leverage and other key risk exposures to the Board at least quarterly; the IRC monitors exposures monthly in this model. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: File the decision record
steps.description: The liquidity principal files the paper, the approval and Risk's comments in the document store so the decision trail is available for audit and the next month's review.

control.basis: Record of management decisions on leverage for internal and external audit

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Projected leverage approaches the Board limit
exceptions.description: The projection shows leverage nearing the limit, so the managing director escalates to the CIO and CFRO and the options are rebuilt around slower deployment or less synthetic exposure.

exceptions.name: Review asks for another option
exceptions.description: Risk, the monthly review or the CIO asks for a different mix, for example more term funding after commercial paper spreads widen.

exceptions.name: Funding market disruption
exceptions.description: As in March 2020, commercial paper cannot be rolled; an extra review shifts funding to term repo and term debt and the plan is reissued within days.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from month end to the filed, approved plan
benchmarks.population: Monthly leverage and funding reviews at a large Canadian pension investment manager

evidence.note: Author's estimate: three to five days for final month-end positions, about a week of analysis and Risk review, a mid-month meeting and CIO approval, then the execution calendar.
18% to 25% of net assets over F2018 to F2022.

pain_points.description: The leverage figure depends on classifying derivatives and repo correctly across systems, so it needs a manual reconciliation with Risk every month.

evidence.note: Recourse leverage combines debt, repo and derivative notionals net of cash and reverse repo.

pain_points.description: Private deployment timing is uncertain, so the projected funding need, and with it the plan, often moves after approval.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; the liquidity forecast notes uncertain private fund call timing.

pain_points.description: Short-term funding can close suddenly in a crisis, so plans that lean on commercial paper must be stress-tested and sometimes redone mid-month.

evidence.note: Loss of US commercial paper access in March 2020.

sources.title: The model fund F2022 Annual Report (fiscal year ended March 31, 2022)
sources.supports: Strategic Portfolios: six asset classes and three regions, indicative allocations five years out (base plan public equity 23%, private equity 23%, public fixed income 32%, credit 17%, real assets 31%, cash and absolute return -27%); strategic mix of factor exposures and leverage reviewed at least triennially; CIO accountable for designing Strategic Portfolios and recommending market risk and leverage targets; ISRC with Portfolio Execution, Portfolio Strategy, Investment Risk and Operational and Legal Risk committees; Business Plan includes the Strategic Portfolios; leverage defined (term debt, commercial paper, secured borrowing, synthetic financing); recourse leverage C$122 billion in F2022, 18% to 25% of net assets over five years; Board limit of 45% of net assets from April 1, 2022, reviewed yearly with risk appetite; 10-day liquidity coverage ratio 2.9x against 1.0x; leverage-related expenses C$295 million. sources.title: The model fund F2021 Annual Report (fiscal year ended March 31, 2021)

sources.title: COVID-19 crisis: Liquidity management at Canada's largest public pension funds (Staff Analytical Note 2021-11)
sources.supports: In March 2020 the eight largest Canadian pension funds, including the model fund, faced margin calls peaking near C$30 billion in one week and lost access to US commercial paper; they increased long-term repos by about C$20 billion, issued about C$19 billion of long-term debt from March to May 2020 and used total return swaps to raise about C$20 billion; leverage and access to funding markets are the two main sources of liquidity risk. Read from a text copy saved under scratch/.

sources.title: Staff Analytical Note 2024-4 (repo market activity)
sources.supports: Canadian pension funds fund large beta fixed income portfolios with repo through primary dealer desks and use repo for daily cash shortfalls and bridge financing of acquisitions. Later than the reference period; used for practice.

assumptions: The monthly review meeting and its chair are the author's assumption; the organisation file says the CIO approves the plan with Risk input.
tfm_associate is added for data and paper work although the process map lists only principals and above.
Term debt execution (dealer mandates, documentation) and daily commercial paper and repo trading are in separate processes; this workflow ends with the execution calendar.
The Board-level leverage limit of 45% applies from April 2022; earlier in the period leverage was governed by the limits in the Risk Policy, which are not published.
Authorised debt limits come from rating agency releases; the body that set them is not stated there.
Loaded costs are taken from the organisation file.
